subject: Biology
title: Morphology of Flowering Plants
summary: Morphology is the study of external form: root, stem, leaf, inflorescence, flower, fruit and seed. Each part is modified in many plants for storage, support, protection or reproduction.
Dicots usually have tap roots and reticulate venation; monocots have fibrous roots and parallel venation.

A flower is a modified shoot. Its parts (calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium) are described by symmetry, aestivation, ovary position and placentation, and summarised in a floral formula and floral diagram.
Three families are studied in detail: Fabaceae (pea), Solanaceae (potato) and Liliaceae (lily).

formulas.name: Root types
formulas.formula: tap root (from radicle — mustard);  fibrous root (wheat);  adventitious (from other parts — grass, Monstera, banyan)

formulas.name: Root modifications
formulas.formula: storage — carrot, turnip (tap), sweet potato (adventitious);  prop roots — banyan;  stilt roots — maize, sugarcane;  pneumatophores — Rhizophora (mangroves)

formulas.name: Stem modifications
formulas.formula: underground storage — potato (tuber), ginger, turmeric (rhizome), Colocasia (corm), onion (bulb);  tendrils — cucumber, grapes;  thorns — Bougainvillea, Citrus;  phylloclade — Opuntia, Euphorbia;  runner — grass;  stolon — mint, jasmine;  offset — Pistia, Eichhornia;  sucker — banana, pineapple, Chrysanthemum
formulas.note: Potato is a stem (has nodes and eyes), sweet potato is a root.

formulas.name: Leaf modifications
formulas.formula: tendrils — peas;  spines — cacti;  fleshy storage — onion, garlic;  phyllode (flattened petiole) — Australian Acacia;  pitcher — Nepenthes;  bladder — Utricularia

formulas.name: Phyllotaxy
formulas.formula: alternate — China rose, mustard, sunflower;  opposite — Calotropis, guava;  whorled — Alstonia

formulas.name: Inflorescence
formulas.formula: racemose: main axis keeps growing, flowers acropetal (older below);  cymose: main axis ends in a flower, flowers basipetal

formulas.name: Flower symmetry and ovary position
formulas.formula: actinomorphic (radial — mustard, Datura, chilli);  zygomorphic (one plane — pea, gulmohur, Cassia);  hypogynous (superior — mustard, China rose, brinjal);  perigynous (half-inferior — plum, rose, peach);  epigynous (inferior — guava, cucumber, sunflower ray florets)

formulas.name: Aestivation
formulas.formula: valvate (Calotropis);  twisted (China rose, lady's finger, cotton);  imbricate (Cassia, gulmohur);  vexillary/papilionaceous (pea, bean)
formulas.when: Arrangement of petals in the bud.

formulas.name: Placentation
formulas.formula: marginal (pea);  axile (China rose, tomato, lemon);  parietal (mustard, Argemone);  free central (Dianthus, Primrose);  basal (sunflower, marigold)

formulas.name: Stamen terms
formulas.formula: epipetalous (attached to petals — brinjal);  epiphyllous (attached to perianth — lily);  monoadelphous (China rose), diadelphous (pea), polyadelphous (citrus)

formulas.name: Floral formula symbols
formulas.formula: Br bracteate, ⊕ actinomorphic, % zygomorphic, ⚥ bisexual, K calyx, C corolla, P perianth, A androecium, G gynoecium; G with a line below = superior ovary, line above = inferior

formulas.name: Solanaceae formula
formulas.formula: ⊕ ⚥ K₍₅₎ C₍₅₎ A₅ (epipetalous) G₍₂₎, superior, swollen placenta with axile placentation

formulas.name: Liliaceae formula
formulas.formula: Br ⊕ ⚥ P₍₃₊₃₎ A₃₊₃ G₍₃₎, superior, trilocular, axile

examples.title: Root or stem?
examples.problem: Ginger grows underground. Is it a root or a stem?
examples.solution: A stem (rhizome): it has nodes, internodes, scale leaves and buds. Roots never bear nodes or buds.

examples.title: Fruit type
examples.problem: What is the edible part of mango and coconut?
examples.solution: Both are drupes. Mango: the fleshy mesocarp. Coconut: the endosperm (and the fibrous mesocarp is coir).

examples.title: Pea flower
examples.problem: Describe the corolla of a pea flower.
examples.solution: Papilionaceous: one large standard (vexillum), two lateral wings (alae) and two fused keel petals; vexillary aestivation.

examples.title: Placentation identification
examples.problem: Ovules on the central axis of a multilocular ovary — which placentation, and one example?
examples.solution: Axile placentation — China rose, tomato or lemon.

examples.title: Economic families
examples.problem: Name one food plant each from Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae.
examples.solution: Fabaceae: gram, arhar, soybean (pulses). Solanaceae: potato, tomato, brinjal. Liliaceae: Asparagus (vegetable); aloe and Colchicum are medicinal, tulip and Gloriosa ornamental.

examples.title: Pneumatophores
examples.problem: Why do mangroves like Rhizophora have pneumatophores?
examples.solution: They grow in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil; pneumatophores grow upwards out of the soil to take in oxygen for respiration.

topics.title: Regions of the root
topics.explain: Root cap at the tip protects the apex; region of meristematic activity (cells divide); region of elongation (cells grow); region of maturation (root hairs absorb water and minerals).

topics.title: The leaf
topics.explain: Parts: leaf base (pulvinus in legumes; sheath in monocots), petiole and lamina. Venation is reticulate in dicots and parallel in monocots. Simple leaves have an undivided lamina; compound leaves are pinnate (neem) or palmate (silk cotton). A bud is present in the axil of a leaf but not of a leaflet.

topics.title: Parts of a flower
topics.explain: Calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens) and gynoecium (carpels). When calyx and corolla are not distinct, they form a perianth (lily). Apocarpous carpels are free (lotus, rose); syncarpous are fused (mustard, tomato).

topics.title: Fruit
topics.explain: A fruit is a mature ovary formed after fertilisation; one formed without fertilisation is parthenocarpic. Fruit wall (pericarp) = epicarp, mesocarp, endocarp.

topics.title: Seed
topics.explain: Dicot seed (bean, gram, pea): seed coat (testa and tegmen), hilum, micropyle, embryo with two cotyledons, radicle and plumule. Monocot seed (maize): endospermic, single cotyledon (scutellum), aleurone layer, coleoptile and coleorhiza.

topics.title: Family features
topics.explain: Fabaceae: tap root with root nodules, pinnately compound leaves with pulvinus, legume fruit. Solanaceae: often hairy stems, berry or capsule fruits, many endospermous seeds. Liliaceae: monocot herbs with bulbs, corms or rhizomes; perianth tepals; capsule or berry fruits.

ratta: Potato = stem tuber;  sweet potato = root.
Pneumatophores — Rhizophora;  stilt — maize;  prop — banyan.
Twisted: China rose, cotton;  vexillary: pea;  valvate: Calotropis.
Marginal pea, axile China rose/tomato, parietal mustard, free central Dianthus, basal sunflower.
Fabaceae: A₍₉₎₊₁ diadelphous;  Solanaceae: epipetalous, swollen placenta;  Liliaceae: P₍₃₊₃₎.
